newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London stocks close at record, others falter.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London stocks close at record, others falter.

text.p: London closed at yet another record on Friday but other European bourses slipped from their peaks as Wall Street was hit by profit-taking after ending at an all-time high the day before.

On currency markets, the dollar hit a four-year high against the yen and approached the psychologically important level of 125 yen before falling back in late trade because of jitters over the possibility of central bank moves to curb its rise.
London, Frankfurt and Paris hit intra-day peaks in early trade on the strength of New York's overnight performance, which cracked the 7,000-point barrier on the Dow Jones average for the first time.
London held most of its gain to close in record territory but Paris floor trade and Frankfurt computerised dealings finished in the minus column on disappointment at Wall Street's unsteady opening.
It had been the Dow's strength, fuelled by low interest rates and non-inflationary economic growth, that had injected new life into the bull run on the big European stock markets.

Friday's negative opening on Wall Street came after the Dow ended up 60.81 points at an all-time high of 7,022.44. The rally capped a breathtaking run that has added 1,000 points to the blue-chip index in just four months.

Europe's biggest stock market, London, suffered the least from New York's bad start, retaining a 0.35 percent profit at the close. The market was also supported by bid activity and strong debt markets.
Traders said the London market was continuing to mirror the Dow's performance but was also exercising restraint.
"I think in London we have to start being very wary about the implications of the Dow moving much higher," said Richard Jeffrey, head of research at Charterhouse Tilney.
"The Dow is approaching the top of its justifiable valuation range, the upside is very limited now and it might be entering dangerous territory."
European bourses are seeing record-breaking runs as low inflation has reduced interest rate pressure and the strong dollar enhances prospects for exporting businesses.
In Frankfurt, floor trade, which ended before Wall Street opened, closed at a record 3,248.18 points, up 18.70, on the DAX index, supported by Wall Street and the stronger dollar.
But after-hours dealing on the computerised IBIS index saw earlier gains wiped out as Wall Street weakened on profit-taking. It closed showing a 0.25 percent loss.
Frankfurt dealers said the market was now liable for further corrections after two weeks of strong gains.
In Paris, stocks turned weaker as investors took profits ahead of the weekend, partly encouraged by Wall Street.
French shares had earlier climbed to an intra-day high of 2,643.98 on the CAC-40 index, building on Thursday's rise of more than one percent. They ended just in the loss column.
On foreign exchanges, the dollar's bull run gained momentum in early trade, touching 124.82 yen and analysts said an assault on 125 was just matter of time.

But the U.S. currency lost ground at the end of the European session and finished little changed from Thursday's close. It was underpinned by robust U.S. asset markets but was wary of any central bank move to counter an extension of this week's sharp rally.

"I think that it (125) is going to be a very difficult psychological level to get through," said Adrian Davies, senior strategist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull here. "There are rumours that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will intervene at 125."
Foreign exchange trade was quiet and U.S. markets were expected to wind down early ahead of a long weekend there. Monday is President's Day.

U.S. economic data, did little to change the underlying picture for the dollar. The market took in its stride an unexpected 0.3 percent drop in U.S. producer prices and unchanged industrial production in January.

"There was nothing in the data today to worry the dollar and even though there been some expectation of correction to this week's dollar gains, it just isn't materialising," said Ian Gunner, economist at Chase Investment Bank.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted at 1.6851 marks and 124.07 yen compared with 1.6877 marks and 124.44 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 13.9 points at 4,341.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended down 0.99 points at 2,627.42.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 18.7 points at 3,248.18.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $343.05 an ounce, compared with Thursday's close of $341.85. Silver was at $5.16.
